Definition: from a compound of G3844 and G2698; something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust):--that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust).
BiblicalUsage: Parakatathēkē is the deposit, the treasure committed to one's keeping. Paul tells Timothy, Keep that which is committed to thy trust; he says he knows whom he has believed and is persuaded He is able to keep that which he has committed unto Him; and he charges Timothy to keep by the Holy Ghost the good thing committed unto thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the deposit runs both ways: I commit the gospel to God's keeping, and God commits the gospel to mine, and both deposits are kept by the same power.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
